College Student Substance Abuse Statistics

blocks.html: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) is continuously conducting research that relates to mental health and addiction. A common focus of their energy is the prevalence of drug and alcohol use among college students. A SAMHSA report from 2011 to 2014 showed that alcohol was the most commonly used substance among college students, followed by marijuana, hallucinogens, prescription pain medication, cocaine, stimulants, inhalants, methamphetamine, and heroin, respectively.

blocks.html: College students who abuse drugs and alcohol can fly under the radar more than those who are not college students. A piece of this is the normalcy of drug and alcohol use on campuses and limited exposure to loved ones who would notice changes to their behavior. College students who struggle with drugs and alcohol may find themselves with academic concerns and potential legal concerns.

Introduction
Why Do College Students Abuse Drugs?

blocks.html: If you are the parent or guardian of a college student struggling with alcohol or drugs, you may wonder why they do what they do. There is a combination of factors that contribute to the use of drugs and alcohol on college campuses.
blocks.text: If you are the parent or guardian of a college student struggling with alcohol or drugs, you may wonder why they do what they do. There is a combination of factors that contribute to the use of drugs and alcohol on college campuses.

blocks.html: One factor contributing to the use of drugs and alcohol on campuses is that it is socially accepted, and often even expected. College is often portrayed as a time for individuals to experiment and learn about themselves. Alcohol and drugs can be used in these situations. Additionally, access to drugs and alcohol on college campuses can be easier than it would be elsewhere.

blocks.html: When young adults go to college, this can be the first opportunity that they have had without supervision from their parents or guardians. This gives them the opportunity to make their own decisions regarding their behaviors. Some students find that without a structured environment, they have a hard time limiting their time using drugs and alcohol, and setting healthy boundaries.

What Are the Benefits of a College Student Addiction Treatment Program?

blocks.html: There are several reasons why a specialized treatment approach for college students can make a difference in their recovery. The biggest reason for this is that with a specialized treatment program, there are changes within the program that reflect the different situations that college students experience. As an example, a college student rehab program would be more understanding of the course load and exam schedules for students who are engaging in treatment.
